3. The petitioner in Writ Petition Nos. 2265-2268 of 2006 and Writ Petition No. 1634 of 2006 is the proprietor of Kaif International and the petitioner in Writ Petition Nos. 9443, 9138, 9137, 9164 of 2005 and Writ Petition Nos. 1932-1936 of 2006 is the proprietor of Creative Chemicals Ltd and the petitioner in Writ Petition No. 1544 of 2005 is the proprietor of Messrs Sikder Salt Industries. 

 5. In writ petition Nos. 9443, 9137, 9138, 9164 of 2005 and writ petition No. 1932-1936 of 2006 the petitioner has challenged the changing of HS Code from 2501.00.24 to 2501.00.29 and lastly in writ petition 1544 the petitioner challenges changing of HS Code No. 2501.00.24 to 2501.00.29. 

 7. Mr Masood R Sobhan, Mrs Fatema S Chowdhury and AKM Faizul Karim, the learned Counsels appearing on behalf of the petitioners in all the petitions after placing the petitions and relevant Annexures, affidavit in opposition and affidavit-in-reply to the affidavit-in-opposition mainly submits that the petitioners industries are VAT listed as chemical industries. They opened Letter of Credit and imported bulk quantity of salt of industrial grade which arrived at different ports on different dates. It has been further submitted that the imported salt for its use as industrial salt was recommended by the Board of Investment with a condition that it should be used as raw material and following the said instruction the salt was used for that purpose. In other words the purpose of bringing bulk quantity of salt is for conversion of the said into denatured salt. The learned Counsel therefore, submits that the recommendation of the Board of Investment with the CRF certificate issued by the SGS is absolutely binding upon the respondent No. 1, NBR and refusal of respondent No. 1 i.e. NBR to assess the different consignment under changed HS Code is absolutely without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect. In support of his contention the learned Counsel placed reliance on the decision of Chairman, NBR vs Beximco Infusion Ltd reported in 51 DLR (AD) 36. In that decision it was decided that scheme of the Act seems to be that the decision of Board of Investment is binding upon the government to implement the same. Mainly on this ground Mr Sobhan submits that in all fairness this Rule should be made absolute. 

 8. Mr Nazmul Huda, the Senior Advocate with Ms Shawkat Ara Begum, the learned Counsel appearing on behalf of respondent No. 5 filed affidavit-in-opposition and respondent No. 1 filed affidavit-in-opposition in writ petition No. 2265 of 2006. Their common contention is that wastage industrial salt in bulk imported by the petitioners is a finished product and also on intermediate product which will be converted into denatured salt the fixation of import duty is done by the government depending upon the import policy for a particular year or years. Since the government within its jurisdiction has fixed the import duty in accordance with import policy, as resolved by the parliament, it cannot be questioned. Both of them placed reliance on the decision of Writ Petition No. 11041 of 2006 in the case of United Salt Industries Ltd vs NBR wherein his lordship Justice ABM Khairul Hoque held that since the imported goods had already been released at the time of issuance of the Rule furnishing differential amount for the changes of HS Code in cash and on furnishing bank guarantee, the entire matter is to assessed by the customs authority on the basis of Valuation Rules, 2000 after giving the petitioner opportunity to explain his case in every possible way. This decision was affirmed by the Appellate Division in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1432 of 2009. In that decision as we have found that the decision cited by the petitioner reported in 51 DLR (AD) 36 referred to above, was not considered. But their Lordships of the Appellate Division in that decision specifically mentioned that the respondent should give all opportunity to the petitioner to present his case at the time of assessment.
